title: Stryker backs CMR Surgical with about $400m, with option to buy the surgical robot maker
key_facts: Stryker is investing roughly $400 million in CMR Surgical, with an option to buy the robotics firm outright.
Stryker becomes the exclusive US sales agent for CMR's Versius platform, a soft-tissue surgical robot; CMR keeps development and sales elsewhere.
The buy option depends on regulatory sign-off and the usual closing conditions.
CMR CEO Massimiliano Colella said the alliance gives Versius Plus a stronger route to market in the US.
The agreement still needs regulatory approval before anything closes.
The companies say hospitals want robotic systems that fit existing operating-room workflows.
quote_evidence: Stryker is pouring roughly $400 million into CMR Surgical, with an option to buy the robotics firm outright and sell its tech across the US.
Stryker will become the exclusive US sales agent for Versius, while CMR keeps the lead on development and sales everywhere else.
For now, the agreement still needs to clear regulatory approval before anything closes.
why_it_matters_hint: A large US medical device maker is buying its way into surgical robotics.
notes: Amount is 'roughly' $400 million per the article.
